title: A mug with a polyhedron on it, and a reply identifying it as "a sphenomegacorona"
summary: On Wed 18 Nov 12:59Z @samantha.wiki posted a photo: "Coincidentally, my mug this morning has polyhedra on it" (37 likes). At 16:39Z @shimmermathlabs.com (Amber, 1,454 followers) quote-posted it with a picture described as "A pink coffee mug with crudely drawn polyhedron of 20 sides": "polyhedron week comes in many forms" (27 likes), and eleven minutes later replied to that with a second picture, "pink coffee mug with nicer polyhedron of 20 sides": "computer, enhance". At 22:36Z @oszillate.bsky.social (75 followers) replied: "…Hold on ma'am, I believe those are squares in the back. I believe you have been sold a sphenomegacorona, one of the classic adulterated bootleg icosahedrons" (1 like). The next morning Amber replied: "i want my money back!" The talk lane's card talk-polyhedra-week lists the two mugs among the week's entries; this card is the reply and its answer.

sensitive: @oszillate.bsky.social is a small account (R7: hero only). @samantha.wiki spoke in the previous episode (featuredPrevious: spoke): the post may be shown, and the account is not cast to speak. @shimmermathlabs.com was shown in the previous episode. In the same chain a member posted a photo that includes their own arm; it is left out as appearance (R1). General knowledge, not from the digest: the sphenomegacorona is a real Johnson solid (J88) with 16 triangular and 2 square faces, and an icosahedron has 20 triangular faces. "ma'am" is the replier's word in the original; no one's gender is asserted by this card.
